ladder.text: 1. Make two windows. Inside tmux, window 1 is for the app. Press prefix + c to open window 2, which is for the recorder. In window 2, run cd ~/project/terminal-project/regionsel.

❯ How do I do the recordings and give it to you? Give me each and every step

  The idea is to keep the app running in one tmux window and run the recorder from a second window. The recorder points at the app's pane by id, so it doesn't disturb the screen.

  1. Make two windows. Inside tmux, window 1 is for the app. Press prefix + c to open window 2, which is for the recorder. In window 2, run cd ~/project/terminal-project/regionsel.

  2. Find the app pane's id. Start the app in window 1 first, then run this from window 2:
  tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id}  #{window_index}.#{pane_index}  #{pane_current_command}  #{pane_width}x#{pane_height}'
  It prints a line such as %3  1.0  node  120x40. The %3 is the pane id. Pane ids don't change while the pane lives, so you only need to look it up again for new panes.

  3. Put the app into the state you want. Switch to window 1 with prefix + 1, set up the screen as described in the list below, then switch back with prefix + 2. The app stays as it was. Avoid anything that animates, such as a spinner or a blinking
  cursor, because the capture is a single frame.

  4. Record it from window 2:
  scripts/record-fixture.sh claude-code response-prose %3
  The arguments are <app> <case> <pane-id>. It prints recorded WxH -> .... If it says "refusing to overwrite", that case name is already used, so pick another.

  5. Check for secrets before moving on. The files will be public in the open-source repo.
  cat tests/fixtures/claude-code/response-prose.ansi
  This shows the screen rendered. Look for API keys, tokens, emails, private repo or company names, and your home path. Then run:
  grep -a -n -i -E 'exampleusr|@|token|secret|password|api[_-]?key|sk-' tests/fixtures/claude-code/response-prose.ansi
  If something sensitive shows up, either re-record after changing what's on screen, or edit the .ansi file in an editor. If you edit, replace the text with the same number of characters (e.g. xxxxx), because column positions matter. Delete both files
  and re-record if it's messy:
  rm tests/fixtures/<app>/<case>.*

  What to record, with exact case names

  ┌─────┬────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  #  │          Command           │                                                                         What to put on screen                                                                          │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 1   │ claude-code response-prose │ A reply with prose long enough to wrap on 2 or more lines, a bullet list, and a fenced code block. Ask Claude something like "explain Rust lifetimes with an example". │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 2   │ claude-code diff           │ A reply where Claude edited a file and the red and green diff is visible. Ask it to make a small edit in a throwaway repo.                                             │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 3   │ claude-code input-box      │ A multi-line draft in the prompt box (use Shift+Enter or \ plus Enter), with a tool-call block visible above it.                                                       │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 4   │ lazygit default            │ The default layout with a file selected, so the diff shows on the right.                                                                                               │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 5   │ k9s pods                   │ The pods table. If you don't have a cluster, skip this one and tell me.                                                                                                │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 6   │ k9s logs                   │ Press l on a pod to open its logs.                                                                                                                                     │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 7   │ btop main                  │ The default view.                                                                                                                                                      │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 8   │ vim split-numbers          │ :vsplit with :set number, a different file in each half.                                                                                                               │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9   │ vim split-nonumber         │ The same, after :set nonumber.                                                                                                                                         │
  ├─────┼────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 10  │ shell ls-and-wrap          │ In a plain zsh pane, run ls -l in a big directory, then echo "$(seq 1 80 | tr '\n' ' ')" so a long line wraps.                                                         │
  └─────┴────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Don't feel you have to do all 10. Items 1 to 4 are the most valuable, and anything you can't run, just skip. Use throwaway content (a scratch repo, a dummy prompt) wherever you can, because then there's nothing to scrub.

  Handing them to me

  When you're done, run this to check what exists:
  ls -la tests/fixtures/*/
  Then tell me which cases you recorded and any that were awkward, e.g. "k9s skipped, btop was mid-animation". I'll read the .ansi files, look at the raw escapes to see what each app emits, choose the probe positions, and generate the snapshots. If
  you're unsure about a recording, record it anyway. It's cheap to delete.

  The UPDATE_FIXTURES step isn't yours to run, because the probes in expected.json are placeholders until I fill them in.
